_note: Narration script for the Hypoglycaemia module (CPP-009-AO v4.1). Lee on eleven_v4, one take, short conversational sentences (re-narrated 14 Oct 2026). Captions use the text here; the prompt starts with [calmly] and spells initialisms out (see tools/video/voice.json).

lines.head: Introduction
sentences: Hypoglycaemia.
What every Ambulance Officer needs to know.

lines.head: What it looks like
sentences: Low blood sugar can look like confusion, altered behaviour and sweating. And it can progress to unconsciousness and seizure.
So measure the BGL on every patient with an altered conscious state or altered cerebral function. That includes trauma, seizures, and especially children.

lines.head: The number
sentences: Normal is usually above 3.5 millimoles per litre for adults and children. For neonates, it's above 2.5.
This protocol applies when the BGL is below 3.5.

lines.head: Least invasive
sentences: The aim is simple.
Use the least invasive treatment that raises the blood glucose.
And start with basic care and life support.

lines.head: Oral glucose
sentences: Two years or older, with a GCS good enough to swallow the paste? A cough is a good sign. Give oral glucose, up to 15 grams.
And request clinical support as appropriate.

lines.head: Glucagon
sentences: Can't give oral glucose, or it hasn't worked? Consult the EOC Clinician.
They may advise intramuscular glucagon.
Six years or older, or 25 kilograms or more? That's 1 milligram.
From two up to six years, or under 25 kilograms, it's half a milligram.

lines.head: Under two years
sentences: Under two years old? Consult the EOC Clinician.
They may advise oral glucose gel, or intramuscular glucagon, half a milligram. And request clinical support.

lines.head: Giving it safely
sentences: Do the medication checks before you prepare it, before you give it, and again after. With a second clinician whenever you can.
Check the medication, the expiry date, and the dose.
For an injection, use the vastus lateralis, on the anterior lateral part of the mid thigh. Not the side of the thigh.

lines.head: After treatment
sentences: If they recover, consider offering complex carbohydrates to eat.
Then provide transport, and notify the receiving facility.

lines.head: Wrap-up
sentences: So. Measure the sugar. Use the least invasive treatment first. And call the EOC Clinician if oral glucose fails.
Now, have a go with the treatment checker on this page.
